en: The Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Seal of Immeasurability of the Illusion-like Samādhi Spoken by the Buddha,
Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Grand Officer of the Court for the Propagation of the Teachings.
Translated by the Imperial Preceptor and Dharma Master Shi Hu, recipient of the purple robe, and others, by imperial decree: Thus have I heard:

At one time, the World-Honored One was staying at the Deer Park in the Abode of the Sages near Vārāṇasī, together with a great assembly of twenty thousand bhikṣus and twelve thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, whose names were as follows:

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Siṃha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Siṃhamati, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Susthitamati, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Viśeṣacintin, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Lokadhara, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Purandara, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Varuṇadeva, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ratnakūṭa, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Guhya, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Bhadrapāla, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vidyuddeva, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantaprabha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Jñānakūṭa, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Anikṣiptadhura, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Amoghadarśin, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrīkumārabhūta, and so forth.

Furthermore, there were twenty thousand devaputras, namely the devaputra Sudharmatā and the devaputra Sumanas, and so forth—all these devaputras dwelt entirely within the Mahāyāna Dharma—and together with countless hundreds of thousands of other great assemblies, they all reverently surrounded the World-Honored One to listen to and receive his preaching of the Dharma.

At that time, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the assembly named Śrīpuṣpākara, who rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in homage, bowed his head to the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"I have a question; I only pray that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, out of compassion, will grant me leave to speak it briefly.
The Buddha said, "Jayaśrīgarbha!"
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, provides illumination for whoever asks questions.
Now, ask whatever you wish; I shall explain it for you.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmaśrīgarbha addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, achieve the five supernormal powers, and obtain the illusion-like samādhi?”

Having attained this samādhi, when the roots of goodness of sentient beings have matured, he immediately manifests transformations according to his own spiritual power as appropriate; following the faith and understanding arising in those sentient beings, he preaches the Dharma for them, causing them to swiftly realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śrīkūṭagarbha, saying: “Excellent,
excellent, Śrīkūṭagarbha!”
You have now asked well about such matters as these.

In the past, you have already drawn near to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, having planted deep roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas, and you are further able to give rise to a heart of compassion for all sentient beings.
“You should listen attentively and apply your minds with great care; I shall now speak for you.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Saṃpuṣpita-kośa received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha said:
“Jayaśrīgarbha! You should know that there is one dharma which, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can fully accomplish, they will immediately attain the illusion-like samādhi.

Having attained this samādhi, when the roots of goodness of sentient beings have matured, they manifest transformations through their own spiritual power as appropriate; according to the faith and understanding arising in those sentient beings, they preach the Dharma for them, causing them to swiftly realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
Jaya-puṣpa-garbha!
That which is called "the one dharma" refers to the dharma of non-reliance.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes this dharma, they will not form the notion of reliance even throughout the three realms; whether internally or externally, they are entirely without reliance. Because of this, they possess right view.
By virtue of right view, one attains right application and right conduct; therefore, one obtains unobstructed wisdom.
Because wisdom is unimpeded, the mind is likewise unimpeded, and from within this unimpeded mind, one initiates right practice.
Jayaśrīgarbha! How is it that a bodhisattva is able to give rise to correct practice?

It means to understand that all phenomena arise entirely from conditions, and that within these conditionally arisen phenomena, there is not even the slightest dharma that exists as a real accumulation.
Why is this? Because those various conditions are all unreal, how could there be any dharma therein that can arise?
If a dharma arises through conditions, it is in fact non-arising; therefore, all dharmas are entirely without arising.

If a bodhisattva can understand all phenomena as being without arising according to reality, they will achieve the path of all bodhisattvas; they will be able to enter into all the faculties, desires, and affairs of sentient beings with a heart of compassion.

Attaining profound faith and understanding, they realize that all phenomena are entirely like illusions and transformations, even to the point of discerning that all phenomena are merely transformative events. Because such discernment is ultimately empty, all phenomena are likewise empty.
Having understood this, one immediately attains the illusion-like samādhi.
Having attained this samādhi, one is even able to cause sentient beings to swiftly realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpākara again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Within this assembly, how many bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have attained this illusion-like samādhi?”
The Buddha said, “Jinapadmagarbha!

Within this assembly now are sixty great beings, such as the Bodhisattva Maitreya and the Youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, all of whom have donned the inconceivable armor and attained this dharma-gate of the illusion-like samādhi.”
Jayaśrīgarbha asked, “In other worlds,
are there also bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained this samādhi?
The Buddha said:

"Jayaśrīgarbha! To the west, beyond hundreds of thousands of koṭis of buddha-fields, there is a world named Sukhāvatī. There dwells a Buddha named Amitābha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides and teaches the Dharma, transforming and guiding sentient beings."

In that buddha-field, there was a bodhisattva named Avalokiteśvara and another bodhisattva named Mahāsthāmaprāpta. Those two bodhisattvas attained this samādhi and, for seven nights, expounded this Dharma-gate for the sake of other bodhisattvas. Having heard it, those bodhisattvas also attained this samādhi.
The Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpākara again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The bodhisattvas in that buddha-field who have attained the illusion-like samādhi must be more numerous than those here.”

Why is this? Because within this buddha-field, the bodhisattvas have not been able to diligently inquire of and receive from the Bodhisattva Maitreya and the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī such a Dharma-gate; therefore, few have attained this samādhi.
The Buddha said, “Jayaśrīgarbha! So it is, so it is; it is just as you have said.”
"In that buddha-field, the bodhisattvas who dwell in the illusion-like samādhi are immeasurable, innumerable, and incalculable.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Saṃkusumitarājendra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

I only pray that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, will manifest appropriate signs of supernatural power so that those two Great Beings from that buddha-field may come to this Sahā world.
Furthermore, he caused the great assembly in this gathering to behold the world of Sukhāvatī and gaze upon the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha. Why was this?

If the sons and daughters of good family within this buddha-field should behold that Tathāgata Amitābha, they will immediately be able to give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, each vowing to be born in that buddha-field, and all shall universally attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Furthermore, if those two Great Beings come to this realm, the roots of goodness of all the sons and daughters of good family who practice the Bodhisattva vehicle in this land will increase; or else, having heard the Dharma taught by those two Great Beings, they will immediately attain the Illusion-like Samādhi.

At that time, having accepted the request of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Saṃkusumitarājendra, the World-Honored One immediately emitted a great radiance from between his eyebrows. That light was golden in color and universally illuminated this trichiliocosm, completely piercing through all mountains, rocks, groves, and places of darkness—including Mount Sumeru, Mount Mucilinda, Mount Mahāmucilinda, the Snowy Mountains, the Cakravāḍa Mountains, and the Mahācakravāḍa Mountains—extending even to the furthest limits of other worlds.
All the light of the sun and moon in the world, though vast and blazing, is eclipsed by the radiance of the Buddha; thus it becomes as minute in scale as the light of an eye.

At that time, the golden light shone with brilliant radiance, penetrating through hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Buddha-fields in the western direction, reaching as far as the realm of Sukhāvatī where the Tathāgata Amitābha resides. Having circled the Buddha seven times, illuminating everything everywhere, the light vanished from before that Buddha and became invisible.

At that time, all the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and other classes of beings in the world of Sukhāvatī, riding upon the aforementioned light, were able to see this Sahā world and behold the Tathāgata Śākyamuni surrounded by his assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas;
it was as if they were looking at an āmalaka fruit in the palm of their hand. They all gave rise to hearts of joy and delight, and spoke these words:
"Namo to the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha!"

At that time, within the assembly of Śākyamuni Tathāgata in this Sahā world, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, Brahmā kings, Śakra, the four world-protecting kings, as well as other devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, were all able to see that Land of Ultimate Bliss, and to see the Tathāgata Immeasurable Light surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas; his radiance was blazing and magnificent like Mount Sumeru, shining through and illuminating this entire realm.
Just as a person with clear vision can observe the surrounding horizon within the span of a single cubit without exerting effort, so too is it with their mutual seeing of one another.

At that time, the assembly in this gathering, having beheld the Buddha and that world with its countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of perfectly adorned and complete merits, all gave rise to hearts of joy, delight, and affection, and spoke these words:
"Homage to the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha of Immeasurable Light!"

When these words were spoken, eighty-four thousand sentient beings within the assembly all resolved their minds upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; by virtue of this root of goodness, they shall be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss.

At that time, all the bodhisattvas and the great assembly of śrāvakas in that world also gave rise to a sense of rare wonder; with palms joined in reverence, they prostrated themselves from afar toward the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and spoke these words again:
“Homage to the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha!”

When these words were spoken, that world of Ultimate Bliss shook in six ways: namely, it quaked, quaked universally, and quaked equally and universally; it trembled, trembled universally, and trembled equally and universally; it crashed, crashed universally, and crashed equally and universally; it surged, surged universally, and surged equally and universally; it roared, roared universally, and roared equally and universally; it thundered, thundered universally, and thundered equally and universally.
After these signs had thus appeared, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, together with the assembly, addressed the Tathāgata Amitābha, saying:
"How marvelous!
World-Honored One! How rare! Sugata!
"By merely reciting the name of that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the great earth can be made to tremble in six ways.
That Buddha said: "O son of good family!"

Not only did such signs appear when the name of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was being extolled within this buddha-field, but in countless other buddha-fields as well, the names of that Buddha were likewise extolled; consequently, those various buddha-fields were touched by the light’s radiance, and each of them shook in six ways.

Within these lands, all the immeasurable and innumerable classes of sentient beings who hear the name of this Tathāgata Śākyamuni will all cause their roots of goodness to increase and shall never regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, among the assembly of bodhisattvas in that gathering, there were forty koṭis of bodhisattvas who, upon hearing the name of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, all made this vow:
"We shall gather all roots of goodness whatsoever and dedicate them entirely toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta went before the Tathāgata Amitābha; each bowed his head at the feet of that Buddha in salutation, gazed upon him with reverent devotion, withdrew to stand to one side, and together addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
The light emitted previously by that Tathāgata Śākyamuni has never before been heard or seen; it is truly rare.
For what cause and condition does he manifest this manifestation of light?
If there were no causes or conditions, that Buddha, the World-Honored One, would not emit this radiance.
What is the matter? We pray that the Buddha will explain it for us.
That Buddha replied:
"Good son! So it is, so it is;
it is just as you have said."

The radiance emitted by the Tathāgata Śākyamuni does not arise without cause or condition; for that Blessed One intends to proclaim the supreme Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva’s abiding in the treasure of samādhi, he first manifests this sign in order to teach the Dharma.
Then the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta again addressed that Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We now wish to go to that Sahā world to behold, pay homage to, and draw near to the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and to hear his preaching of the Dharma.”
"I only pray that you will compassionately grant me your permission. The Buddha said, "Good son!..."
“You all may go; now is precisely the right time.
Because you go, you shall further inspire that Buddha, the World-Honored One, to proclaim the essentials of the Dharma.
At that time, having received the Buddha’s permission, the two Bodhisattvas looked toward the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas and addressed eighty-four koṭis of Bodhisattvas, saying:
“Sons of good family!
We shall now go to the Sahā world to behold, pay homage to, and draw near to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and to listen to his preaching of the Dharma.”

Why is this so? Because that Buddha, the World-Honored One, is most supreme and rare; he is able to perform what is difficult to do, having relinquished other pure and magnificent buddha-lands to delight in the defiled and evil land of the Sahā world, teaching and transforming sentient beings through the power of his great compassionate vows.

Those sentient beings mostly give rise to inferior inclinations and resolutely manifest various karmic afflictions such as greed, hatred, and delusion; yet the Buddha, the World-Honored One, is able to achieve the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* amidst them—this is what makes it a difficult feat.
"You all should follow me and go there.
At that time, the bodhisattvas rejoiced and complied.
Furthermore, within the assembly, there were great śrāvakas who, with one voice and in unison, came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If even those who merely hear the name of that Tathāgata Śākyamuni obtain such excellent benefit, how much more so for those who go in person before him to gaze upon and pay homage?”
"May those who gaze upon and pay homage to you have their physical eyes purified; we wish to go there, and pray that the Buddha will grant us permission.
The Buddha said, "You may go; now is precisely the right time."
At that time, eighty-four koṭis of bodhisattvas, together with the great śrāvakas, respectfully surrounded Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva as they came to the Sahā world.
As the Bodhisattva proceeded, he manifested various physical forms and miraculous deeds as was appropriate for each occasion.

At that time, eighty-four koṭis of bodhisattvas each miraculously manifested eighty-four koṭis of exquisite pavilions; each pavilion was twelve yojanas high and eight yojanas wide, beautifully adorned on all four sides and corners.

These pavilions were composed of the seven treasures—gold, silver, vaidūrya, crystal, ruby, agate, and amber; some were made of gold and silver; some of gold, silver, and vaidūrya; some of gold, silver, vaidūrya, and agate; some of gold, silver, vaidūrya, agate, and crystal;

and some of gold, silver, vaidūrya, crystal, amber, and ruby. Some were made of red sandalwood, nāgavṛkṣa sandalwood, and aloeswood sandalwood; others were composed of a combination of various exquisite varieties of sandalwood and the like.
Some are composed of *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers;
some are composed of *sumana*, *vārṣika*, *campaka*, *pāṭala*, and *atimuktaka* flowers; and some are composed of *dhānu*.
Some are composed of *sṛgā* flowers; some are composed of *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava* flowers;
some are composed of *mañjūṣaka*, *mahāmañjūṣaka*, *rūcaka*, *mahārūcaka*, *cakravartin*, *mahācakravartin*, and *surabhi* flowers.
Cakra flowers, mahāsura-cakra flowers, jñāna flowers, mahājñāna flowers,
surabhi-jñāna flowers, jñānulotpa flowers, sāgara flowers, mahāsāgara flowers, and surabhi-sāgara flowers.
Some are composed of various flowers and the like;
some are formed by the adornment of all manner of exquisite flowers;
and some are formed by the adornment of hundreds of thousands of countless, wondrous colors and forms.
In this manner, within each and every pavilion, eighty-four thousand pure radiances all appeared.
The *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Immeasurable Seal of the Illusion-like Samādhi Spoken by the Buddha*, Volume One.
The *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Immeasurable Seal of the Illusion-like Samādhi Spoken by the Buddha*.
In this fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma (Shi Hu),

Court Attendant of the Third Rank, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Dharma-Transmitting Master, and Purple-Robed Subject, et al., under imperial decree: Furthermore, surrounding each of those pavilions, there are some celestial maidens holding various musical instruments— namely, the pipa, the bi-li, the qin, the sheng, the kong-hou, conch shells, drums, small drums, and clappers— and they perform exquisite music.
Some celestial maidens held powdered red candana sandalwood;
some celestial maidens held powdered nāgavṛkṣa candana sandalwood; some celestial maidens held powdered agaru candana sandalwood;
some celestial maidens held powdered black agaru candana sandalwood; or some celestial maidens...
Some held powdered sandalwood of various exquisite qualities;
some celestial maidens held *utpala*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers;
some celestial maidens held *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava* flowers; and some celestial maidens held *parūṣaka* and *mahāparūṣaka* flowers.
Some held *ruṣaka* flowers; some goddesses held *mañjūṣaka* and *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers;
some goddesses held *ruca* and *mahāruca* flowers; some goddesses held *cakra*, *mahācakra*, and *samantacakra* flowers.
There were *sruñjīra* flowers and *kṛta* flowers; some goddesses held *candana* flowers, *mahācandana* flowers, and *sruñjīracandana* flowers;
others held *sattala* flowers, *mahāsattala* flowers, and *sruñjīrasattala* flowers.
Some held divine flowers;
others held celestial garments, exquisite flowers, exquisite incense, unguents, powdered incense, and so forth, remaining stationed in their respective places.
Within each of those pavilions, there was a lion throne adorned with great, wondrous jewels, upon which an emanation of the Tathāgata sat, fully endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man.
Furthermore, within each and every pavilion, eighty-four thousand pearl necklaces were manifested; these pearls were of three colors: blue, white, and red.

Furthermore, within each and every pavilion, eighty-four thousand exquisite and wonderful jeweled banners were manifested; they were covered above with nets of golden bells, and celestial garments hung down as ornamental adornments.
Furthermore, within each and every pavilion, eighty-four thousand precious vases were manifested, filled with various exquisite fragrances.

Moreover, within each and every pavilion, eighty-four thousand supreme and wonderful precious canopies were manifested, adorned with hundreds of thousands of varieties of most exquisite colors and patterns.

Furthermore, within each and every pavilion, eighty-four thousand rows of tāla trees and eighty-four thousand rows of trees made of the seven precious gems were manifested, each adorned with jeweled cords interlaced together.

Furthermore, within each and every pavilion, eighty-four thousand jeweled nets with suspended bells were manifested; when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced harmonious and elegant sounds like those of hundreds of thousands of kinds of exquisite music.

Furthermore, within each and every pavilion, there appeared transformed jeweled ponds. These ponds had bottoms entirely covered with golden sand and were bordered by paths made of the seven treasures, adorned on all sides with lapis lazuli and crystal. They were filled with water possessing the eight virtues, and from within them grew blue lotuses (*utpala*), red lotuses (*padma*), yellow lotuses (*kumuda*), and white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*). Moreover, these ponds resounded with the harmonious calls of various exotic birds, such as ducks, geese, and mandarin ducks.
Eighty-four thousand exquisite jewel-trees surrounded it on all sides, adorned above by eighty-four thousand jeweled cords interlaced as ornaments.
Furthermore, from within each and every pavilion, a great radiance issued forth, illuminating eighty-four thousand yojanas in width.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and the assembly of bodhisattvas who had come from those places, simultaneously placed all those exquisite and wonderful adornments of the various pavilions within a single pavilion; yet these various adornments did not obstruct one another.
It was as if a strong man could reach this Sahā world in the mere time it takes to bend and extend his arm.

By means of their supernormal powers, the bodhisattvas each brought forth eighty-four koṭis of exquisite pavilions adorned with meritorious virtues and placed them within the Buddha’s assembly. Through the appropriate power of their supernormal feats, they caused this Sahā world to become as level as the palm of a hand, yet the Buddha’s assembly was not crowded at all.
From these various pavilions issued forth a great radiance that illuminated this trichiliocosm.

At that time, those two bodhisattvas approached the Buddha, prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to stand to one side. Together they addressed the Buddha, saying:

"The Tathāgata Amitābha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, sends his greetings to the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, inquiring whether you have little illness and little affliction, whether your movements and activities are light and easy, and whether you are dwelling in peace and happiness."
Those two bodhisattvas again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“We bodhisattvas and śrāvakas have come to behold and pay our respects to the Buddha, the World-Honored One, because we saw him in the world of Sukhāvatī.”

At that time, within the assembly of the Buddha in this Sahā world, all the bodhisattvas and the great multitude of śrāvakas, having seen this world purified and adorned, as well as the countless vast and lofty pavilions, all gave rise to this thought:
"For what reason does the Tathāgata manifest such majestic power, enabling those great bodhisattvas to come here?"
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpākara, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and addressed him, saying: “It is rare,
World-Honored One!”
"How marvelous,
O Sugata! Is this adornment of the Sahā world and the manifestation of these pavilions due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata?"
"Is this a transformation produced by the majestic power of those two bodhisattvas?
We pray that the Buddha will explain it for us.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Padmaśrīgarbha, saying:

"Jayaśrīgarbha! This is not through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata, but rather it is a manifestation produced by the awesome power of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta; therefore, this sign has appeared."
Jayaśrīgarbha again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How rare it is,
World-Honored One!"
"How marvelous, O Sugata!

These two great beings have already attained the purity of inconceivable power of aspiration and the stainless whiteness of their roots of goodness; it is only thus that they can possess such supernatural powers and majesty."
The Buddha said to Jñānākara: "So it is, so it is; it is just as you have said.
These two great beings have, over hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of eons, accumulated roots of goodness that are pure and immaculate."
Furthermore, having already attained the dharma-gate of the illusion-like samādhi, from within this samādhi, they are able to manifest various such phenomena as physical forms and supernormal powers.
Furthermore, Vijayagarbha! Let this matter rest for a moment; observe the eastern direction—what signs do you perceive there?

Vijayagarbha Bodhisattva, receiving the Buddha’s holy command, immediately used his unimpeded, pure divine eye to behold the eastern direction. Within as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, he saw as many Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as there are grains of sand in the Ganges. Before each and every Buddha, there were the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, both of whom prostrated at the feet of the Buddhas. Furthermore, he heard them say:

"The Tathāgata Amitābha, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, sends his greetings to the World-Honored One, inquiring whether you have little illness and little affliction, whether your movements are light and easy, and whether you are dwelling in peace and happiness."
He also saw immeasurable, vast multi-storied pavilions exquisitely adorned with wonderful jewels.

Likewise, in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—in each of these—he saw within Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Before each of those Buddhas stood two Great Beings, each prostrating at the Buddha’s feet, and he heard them say:

“The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha sends his greetings to the World-Honored One: Are you free from illness and affliction? Is your movement and rest light and easy? Do you dwell in peace and happiness?”
Furthermore, he saw immeasurable, vast multi-storied pavilions exquisitely adorned with wonderful jewels.
Having seen these signs, the Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpadanta again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How rare! How extraordinary!”
World-Honored One! How rare!
Well-Gone One!

These two great beings have truly attained the most supreme gate of illusion-like samādhi; they are able to manifest their bodies throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, and their supernatural powers and majestic might are inconceivable.
At that time, the World-Honored One surveyed the assembled multitude and manifested signs of supernatural power according to their respective needs.

Immediately, by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, the entire assembly became like the Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpākara: they were able to see the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and before each of those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, they saw two Great Beings, each prostrating at the Buddha’s feet, and even beheld those vast palatial towers adorned with exquisite jewels.
When this assembly beheld these signs, thirty-two thousand beings within the gathering resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Saṃkusumitarājendra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Under which Buddha did these two Great Beings first resolve their minds toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
How long has it been since you first resolved your mind [for enlightenment]?
What is the name of that Buddha-Tathāgata?

We pray that the World-Honored One will graciously explain this for us, so that other bodhisattvas may know what he has cultivated and how he has practiced, and thereby ultimately attain the fulfillment of their own vows and conduct.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpadanta, saying:
“Listen attentively and apply your mind with great care; I shall now speak for you.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpadanta received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha said to Śrīkūṭagarbha:

"In the past, incalculable upon incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, and further through vast, immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable numbers of kalpas—having passed beyond these kalpas—if one were to shatter this trichiliocosm into fine motes of dust, and let each mote represent one kalpa, then prior to the passing of those dust-mote kalpas, there was a world named Universal Manifestation of Wondrous Joy Adorned with Immeasurable Merit-Jewels. A Buddha appeared in that world, titled Siṃhavikrīḍita-kanakaprabharāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."
In that buddha-field, all matters such as its meritorious adornments are vast and immeasurable.
Śrīkūṭaraśmiprabhāsa! What do you think?
"Are all the meritorious adornments within that world of Sukhāvatī, belonging to that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha, not many?"
Jayaśrīgarbha said: “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"It is immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable.
The Buddha said to Śrīkūṭagarbha,
"I shall briefly clarify this meaning through a parable."
Suppose, for example, there were a person who took a single hair, split it into one hundred parts, and from one of those parts drew a single drop of water from the great ocean.
O Saṃkusumitarāja!
What do you think? Is that water on the tip of the hair more abundant,
or is the water of the great ocean more abundant?
Jaya-puṣpa-garbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The water on the tip of a hair is extremely minute, whereas the remaining great oceans are immeasurable in depth and breadth.”
The Buddha said to Jyotīrasa:
"You should now know that all the merits, adornments, and other matters of the world of Sukhāvatī belonging to the Tathāgata Amitābha are like water on the tip of a hair;

whereas all the merits, adornments, and other matters of the world of Universal Manifestation of Wondrous Joy belonging to the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍita-golden-light-king are like the waters of the great ocean."

Furthermore, the assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas in the gathering of the Tathāgata King of Golden Light Sporting Like a Lion is hundreds of thousands of times greater than that of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Light; that Buddha, the World-Honored One, expounds the Dharma of the Three Vehicles according to their capacities.

Jayaśrīgarbha! To speak briefly, regarding all the meritorious adornments and sublime delights within the buddha-field of that Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitaghoṣarāja, even if I were to employ my eloquence extensively throughout kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, I would still be unable to describe their limits.
"Furthermore, Jinaśrīgarbha!

Within the Dharma of that Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitakāñcanaprabharāja, there was a king named Jayasena. That king was preeminent and sovereign over a thousand worlds, possessing vast wealth and prosperity; he governed the world through the True Dharma.
He had seventy-six thousand supreme gardens for his own enjoyment, and each of the king’s sons likewise enjoyed ten thousand parks."
The Bodhisattva Jyotirśrīgarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Are there women in that buddha-field?”
The Buddha said, “No, son of good family!”
In that buddha-field, even the name "woman" cannot be heard, let alone the existence of women.

Those born there are all of miraculous birth (upapāduka), pure and pristine, and all practice the holy life (brahmacarya). All sentient beings take the joy of the Dharma and the bliss of dhyāna as their sustenance, and do not consume any coarse or impure solid food.
Jaya-kuśala-garbha!
For eighty-four thousand koṭis of years, that king and his son honored and made offerings to the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍita-suvarṇaprabhāsa-rāja.
When that Buddha, the World-Honored One, knew that the king’s profound mind had given rise to pure faith, he immediately expounded for him the Dharma-gate of Skillfulness in the Infinite Seal.
"Vijayaprabhāsa! What is called the Dharma-gate of Skillfulness in the Infinite Seal?"
This refers to the various practices undertaken by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, which never seek or aspire toward limited phenomena. Why is this?

Because these bodhisattvas practice immeasurable giving, immeasurable ethical discipline, immeasurable patience, immeasurable diligence, immeasurable meditative concentration, and immeasurable wisdom; they enter into immeasurable cycles of birth and death, extend compassion to immeasurable sentient beings, adorn immeasurable buddha-lands, adorn immeasurable assemblies of śrāvakas, perfect immeasurable physical forms, and are endowed with immeasurable voices and immeasurable eloquence.

"Jayaśrīgarbha! Even the roots of goodness arising from a single moment of resolve by Bodhisattvas are dedicated toward all things with immeasurable and vast minds; how much more so when they have accumulated immeasurable practices and vows, universally dedicating them for the sake of all sentient beings, so that all beings may fully realize non-arising and attain nirvāṇa just as the Buddha does in his parinirvāṇa."
"Good son! This is called the 'Infinite Dedication.

Because of this dedication, emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are all infinite; suchness, the limit of reality, and the dharma-realm are likewise infinite; it is liberation, non-arising, and freedom from all attachments."
Good son! To state it briefly, that which is called "immeasurable meanings" refers to the immeasurability of all phenomena (*dharma*).
For what reason is it said that all phenomena are immeasurable?
Because all phenomena are without arising and without cessation, they are immeasurable.

If a phenomenon is immeasurable, it is without arising and without cessation; if a phenomenon is without arising and without cessation, it is immeasurable. This is called the Dharma-gate of the Seal of Immeasurability.

“Jayaśrīgarbha! At that time, when the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitajagadvirocanaghoṣarāja expounded this Dharma-gate of the skillful means of the infinite seals for King Jayasena, the king attained awakening to all phenomena.”
"Furthermore, Śrīgarbha! That King Śrīmān practiced the cultivation of meditative concentration within the Buddha-dharma.

Later, at one time, while he was settled in meditative concentration, two lotus flowers—extraordinarily beautiful and lovely, pure like *nāgakesara* and sandalwood—suddenly grew from his left and right flanks. From within those flowers, two youths appeared, sitting cross-legged."
Upon seeing this, the king marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence and spoke these verses to the youth:
"Are you perhaps a deva or a nāga? Or are you of the yakṣa or rākṣasa kind?
Are you a human, a non-human, or a ṛṣi?"
"What name do you ask me to declare?
Then the youth born from the right side immediately spoke a verse in reply to the king:
"Within the emptiness of all phenomena, You now ask me what my name is."
Yet those dharmas are fundamentally nameless; for what reason are you asking about them by means of names?
Within the emptiness of dharmas, there are no devas or nāgas, nor are there yakṣas or rākṣasa types, humans or non-humans, or even ṛṣis—all such things are utterly non-existent.
Then the youth born from the left side also spoke a verse in reply to the king, saying:
“The name and the named entity are both empty; The namer and the named are likewise non-existent.
Within all phenomena, which are devoid of names, One expresses them only by means of forced designations.”
Know that the true name is the intrinsic nature; herein there is neither seeing nor hearing.
It is primordially without cessation and without arising; why then do you ask about seeing by means of names?

Whatever names there are for all things that are done, since they are expressed by means of provisional designations, I too shall now employ provisional designations: the first name is Ratnavyūha, and the second is Ratnottama.

After those two youths had spoken these verses, by the power of their past roots of goodness, they attained the five supernormal powers and immediately went together with King Jyotiṣprabha to the presence of the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitavairocana.
Having arrived, they each prostrated with their heads at the feet of the Buddha, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to stand to one side.
Those two youths joined their palms toward the Buddha and, in unison, spoke these verses:
"With what things shall we now make an offering To the Perfectly Awakened One, the Honored One among bipeds?"
I pray that the Buddha will open my mind regarding this matter, so that upon hearing it, my heart may find peace.
Now I have neither flowers nor incense; I lack food, drink, and clothing;
I possess none of the various exquisite offerings—what then shall I offer to the Most Victorious One?
At that time, the Buddha spoke these verses for the two youths:
"If one can give rise to the bodhicitta even once, Bringing vast benefit and happiness to all sentient beings,
This is what is called the true offering To the Perfectly Awakened One who possesses the thirty-two marks."
If a person were to fill as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in the Ganges with the most excellent and wondrous flowers,
and offer them to the World-Honored One, the Savior of the World; yet if another person, with a sincere heart,
merely joins their palms and gives rise to the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment— [the latter's merit would be far greater].
The superior gateway of merit obtained by this person is many times greater than before, beyond measure.
Apart from this, what could be called true offering?
Apart from this, what could be called the supreme reliance?
"If a person can give rise to the bodhicitta, I declare them to be a person of supreme wisdom.
Thus ends the middle fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-māyopama-samādhi-apramāṇa-mudrā-dharmaparyāya-sūtra*.
The *Buddhabhāṣita-māyopama-samādhi-apramāṇa-mudrā-dharmaparyāya-sūtra*.
Fascicle Lower.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Court-Attendant of the Third Rank, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Grand Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Purple-Robed Subject Shi Hu, et al., by Imperial Decree. "Furthermore, Jinaśrīgarbha!
At that time, those two youths addressed the Buddha, the World-Honored One, with these verses:
“The Capable Sage utters the great lion’s roar, Which all devas and humans everywhere hear.
Now, before the presence of the World-Honored One, We each make our most supreme and sincere vows:”
Until the very end of the future, may my practice throughout many kalpas involve entering the cycle of birth and death to deliver countless classes of sentient beings.
By this cause and condition, we now shall contemplate [this] throughout the limits of the future;
for the sake of universally benefiting and gladdening all sentient beings, we shall practice without weariness through boundless eons.
From this day forward, we shall forever extinguish the defilements of greed, hatred, and delusion;
may the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently residing throughout the ten directions, bear witness that what I have spoken is true and without falsehood.
We now resolve to attain bodhicitta, taking no pleasure in the fruits of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
if we were to delight in such inferior minds, we would certainly incur the retribution of false speech.
I do not delight in the fruits of the two vehicles; driven solely by compassion for sentient beings, even throughout many koṭis of kalpas, may I always practice without weariness.
Just as the Buddha, the World-Honored One, has achieved, and just as the Buddha-fields are extensively adorned according to his merit,
may I, when I attain Buddhahood in the future, possess Buddha-lands many times more than ten million in number.
Furthermore, I vow that in the Buddha-fields of the future, there shall be no assembly of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas;
they shall be adorned solely by bodhisattvas, who have extensively gathered immeasurable accumulations of wisdom.
May I, having attained such adornments, cause all sentient beings to be free from defilement;
born from the teachings of all Buddhas, may they universally uphold the treasury of the Buddha-dharma.
If what I have now spoken is true, without falsehood or variation,
may this great ocean and the mountains and rivers, even unto the great earth, all tremble.
When these words of aspiration were uttered, the great earth immediately shook in every direction;
musical instruments, though unstruck, resounded spontaneously, emitting subtle and wondrous sounds that pervaded the ten directions.
The heavens rained down a multitude of flowers and exquisite fragrances, most magnificent, beautiful, and exceedingly lovely.
"Hundreds of thousands of millions of exquisite celestial garments were scattered everywhere in profusion.
At that time, those two youths each gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
Jayaśrīgarbha! What do you think?
Was the King Jayatejas at that time someone other than this person?
He is none other than the present Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha.
At that time, the youth Ratnavyūha was the present Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, and the youth Ratnottama was the present Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
These two bodhisattvas first gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the presence of that Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitavairocanarāja.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Padmaśrīgarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

These two Great Beings are truly rare; such names as theirs are difficult even to hear, yet they are fully endowed with profound faith and understanding, and the bodhicitta they have generated is beyond compare."
“World-Honored One!
After the Tathāgata Golden Light King of Lion’s Play, how many other Buddhas did these two great beings further make offerings to?
The Buddha said:

“Good son! One might still be able to know the limit and the number of all the sands of the Ganges River, but I cannot know the limit of the Tathāgatas whom these two great beings have made offerings to after that Buddha.
Why is this? Because these two great beings have both donned the inconceivable armor and are fully endowed with immeasurable, sublime merits; therefore, it is impossible to know their limits.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śrīkūṭagarbha again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
in which direction lies that world-system called Immeasurable Merit Jewel-Adorned Universal Manifestation of Sublime Joy?”
The Buddha said,
“Good son! This present Western World of Ultimate Bliss is none other than that World of Universal Manifestation of Wondrous Joy, Adorned with Jewels of Immeasurable Merit, of the past.”
Jayaśrīgarbha said: "At what time shall these two Great Beings realize the fruit of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
And what kind of meritorious adornments of a buddha-field shall they attain?"
Furthermore, what is the measure of the Buddha’s lifespan?
And how many is the assembly of bodhisattvas?

We pray that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, out of vast compassion for the benefit and happiness of all the world’s devas and humans, will proclaim the future buddhahood of these two great beings, so that other bodhisattvas, having heard this, may all attain the fulfillment of their great vows.
The Buddha said:
"Jayaśrīgarbha! You should listen well and pay close attention; I shall now speak for you."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Padmaśrīgarbha received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha said: "Good son!

It should be known that the lifespan of the Tathāgata Amitābha in the western quarter is immeasurable and utterly incalculable; even in the course of hundreds of thousands of koṭi-nayuta kalpas, one could not describe its limit.

The True Dharma of that Buddha shall remain in the world for eighty-four thousand nayutas of kalpas. After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, by the power of the roots of goodness of all sentient beings, they will likewise encounter other Buddhas appearing in the world; meanwhile, those bodhisattvas, dwelling securely in the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*, shall constantly behold the Buddhas without interruption.

"Good son! Furthermore, after the Tathāgata Amitābha had entered parinirvāṇa, at the site where he had preached the Dharma, there was a wondrous lotus tree adorned with the seven precious gems that spontaneously produced the subtle and sublime sounds of the Dharma. After one night until the time of dawn, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, beneath a bodhi tree adorned with various jewels, sat upon his seat and attained equal and perfect enlightenment."

Having attained perfect enlightenment, he was named the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, known as Samantaprabhā-abhyudgata-śrī-kūṭarāja.

Jayaśrīgarbha! As for the matters concerning the meritorious adornments of that buddha-field, even if I were to employ skillful metaphors and words throughout kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, I could not describe even a small fraction of them.
Furthermore, noble son!

If one were to compare the meritorious adornments of such a buddha-field with the meritorious adornments of the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitagoldenlight King, the former would not equal even a hundredth part; it would not equal a thousandth, a hundred-thousandth, nor any numerical fraction, metaphorical fraction, or even a *upaniṣad* fraction. It would not equal even a single part.
Furthermore, in that land there are no names for śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; it consists solely of a pure assembly of great bodhisattvas.
Moreover, son of good family!

If one were to take the entire assembly of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas from the gathering of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Light and combine them all together to compare them, the assembly of bodhisattvas in the gathering of the Tathāgata Universal Radiance, Exalted and Auspicious King of Peaks, would still be twice as numerous.
The lifespan of that Buddha will be ninety-six koṭi-nayuta-hundred-thousand kalpas, and the True Dharma will remain in the world for sixty koṭi kalpas.
The Bodhisattva Saṃkusumitarājendra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"Is that Buddha-world not also named 'Ultimate Bliss'? The Buddha said, "No."
"Good son! That world is named Universal Adornment of All Jewels.

That Buddha-Tathāgata brings about all manner of benefit and happiness according to what is appropriate for each being. Within that Dharma, this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta remains in the world for as long as the lifespan of that Buddha lasts, serving and making offerings to him. Even after that Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, he upholds the Buddha-Dharma, ensuring that the Dharma remains for a long time. Finally, when the Dharma is on the verge of extinction, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta shall attain the fruit of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi within that land."

Having attained perfect enlightenment, he was named the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, known as Guṇaratnakūṭarāja.

All the merits, adornments, and other such matters within that buddha-field are fully possessed by the assembly of bodhisattvas; the lifespan of that Buddha and the duration of his True Dharma remaining in the world are exactly equal to those of the Tathāgata Samantaprabhābhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja, being entirely complete, neither increasing nor decreasing.
Furthermore, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śrīpuṣpadharakūṭarāja, saying:

“You should now know that if any son or daughter of good family should even briefly hear the names of the Tathāgata Samantaprabhābhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja and the Tathāgata Supratiṣṭhitaguṇaratnakūṭarāja, such a person shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.”
Furthermore, Śrīpuṣpagarbha!

If any son or daughter of good family hears the names of the Tathāgata Past Lion’s Play Golden Light King, the Tathāgata Future Universal Radiance Exalted Auspicious Peak King, and the Tathāgata Well-Abiding Merit Jewel Peak King, then within their respective villages and clans, all women shall transform their female bodies into male ones. For forty koṭis of kalpas, they shall turn their backs on birth and death; in their successive births, they shall attain pure renunciation, constantly behold the Buddhas, hear the Dharma, and serve the Saṅgha. In every life they are born into, they shall possess the knowledge of past lives, as well as obtain dhāraṇīs and unimpeded eloquence, never regressing from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken these words, ninety-six koṭis of devas and humans in the assembly spoke with one voice, saying:

"Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time, and to the Tathāgata Samantaprabha-udgata-śrī-kūṭarāja and the Tathāgata Guṇasuvyavasthita-ratnakūṭarāja of future ages! We rejoice in all the merits and benefits of all the Buddhas; we all resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Immediately, all the Buddhas conferred upon them this prediction, saying:
"You shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, seven thousand bodhisattvas within the assembly attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*); eighty-four nayutas of sentient beings were distanced from dust and free from defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye; and eight thousand bhikṣus, being without further outflows (*āsrava*), attained liberation of mind.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, having manifested various physical forms and miraculous feats within this assembly as was appropriate, were seen by the entire multitude.

At that time, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya worlds in the ten directions, seeing such signs and hearing the proclamation of how those two bodhisattvas were to attain Buddhahood, all praised him together, saying:
"How rare, World-Honored One Śākyamuni Tathāgata!"
“We Buddhas shall also collectively praise these two bodhisattvas, who are able to skillfully protect and sustain them.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Saṃkusumitarājendra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If a son or daughter of good family is able to receive, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain for others such a profound and subtle sūtra as this proclaimed by the Buddha, how much merit will they obtain?
The Buddha said: "Stop, stop!
Son of good family!"
Do not ask such a question.
Why is this? Because those with inferior faith and understanding cannot give rise to faith in such profound sūtras spoken by the Buddha; therefore, I do not speak of them.
The Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpākara addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Within this assembly there are also many sons and daughters of good family who possess vast and profound faith and understanding. We only pray that the Tathāgata will briefly proclaim the merits of upholding [this teaching], so as to serve as a great illumination for all sentient beings in the future final age.”
The Buddha said to Jñānākara:
“Listen attentively, listen attentively!
I shall now speak for you.”
Then the Bodhisattva Jālinīprabha received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha said: "Good son!
Suppose there were a person of great power, fully endowed with merit, who could thoroughly understand the divisions of the realms of sentient beings and speak these words:

"As the Buddha has taught, worlds are boundless and sentient beings are inexhaustible; I am able to carry all those sentient beings upon my head and shoulders for immeasurable and limitless *koṭi* kalpas, and furthermore, I can provide them everywhere with food, drink, clothing, and all articles of pleasure."
"Śrīpuṣpākara! What do you think? Would this person, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?
Śrīpuṣpākara addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Very much, World-Honored One!
If someone were to give rise to a mind of loving-kindness toward even a single sentient being for as long as a finger-snap, they would still gain much merit; how much more so in such a case?”
The Buddha said, “Jayaśrīgarbha!
I now tell you this in truth:

if there are sons or daughters of good family who, regarding this profound sutra, can personally give rise to faith and encourage others to believe in it, the merit they obtain shall be many times greater than that.”

Furthermore, if there is anyone who can receive, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain this profound sutra for others, it should be known that such a person takes the bodhicitta as their foundation.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Padmaśrīgarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Regarding such profound sūtras as those spoken by the Tathāgata—whether during the Buddha’s presence or after his parinirvāṇa—I shall receive, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain them to others, proclaiming and disseminating them so that they shall never be interrupted.”
When the Bodhisattva Śrīpuṣpagarbha had spoken these words, ninety-six koṭis of bodhisattvas in the assembly spoke with one voice, saying:
“World-Honored One!
“We, too, shall receive, uphold, recite, and extensively explain for others the profound sutras spoken by the Buddha.

At that time, Mahābrahmā, Lord of the Sahā World; Śakra, Lord of Devas; the Four World-Protecting Kings; and countless other hosts of devaputras each scattered celestial māndārava flowers over the Buddha and celestial flowers upon the bodhisattvas. They further made hundreds of thousands of koṭis of kinds of exquisite celestial music as an offering.
Furthermore, they spoke these words:

"All sentient beings who hear such a profound and correct Dharma will receive its light universally illuminating them and attain great and wholesome benefit; we shall all receive, uphold, proclaim, and disseminate this Dharma-gate."
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is,
O sons of good family!"
It is as you have said.

This True Dharma is inconceivable; only those who have deeply planted roots of goodness before ten thousand Buddhas will find this sutra fall into their hands, let alone those who are able to receive, uphold, read, recite, and give rise to faith and understanding!
Furthermore, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Puṣpakuṭa, saying:
“If anyone hears this True Dharma, in whatever place they may be, all women shall be transformed into men, with the sole exception of two types: those who are stingy and those who are jealous.”
At that moment, there was a woman in the assembly named Viraja who, having conceived faith and understanding, rose from her seat, approached the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I have now extinguished stinginess and envy within my inner mind, and I have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
If this resolve of mine is true and without falsehood, may I attain Buddhahood; and as the Buddha has spoken, may I immediately transform out of this female form wherever I hear this Dharma.
"If this matter is true, may I, upon changing my rebirth, attain the body of a man.
As soon as that woman had spoken these words, she immediately attained the transformation into a male body.

At that time, the Buddha bestowed upon him the prediction of non-retrogression toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, declaring that he shall attain Buddhahood and be known by the name Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sarvakleśaprahāṇa (The One Who Eliminates All Afflictions).

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas such as Saṃkusumitarājendra, along with the assembly of bhikṣus, and all those present in the great gathering—including gods, humans, asuras, and others—having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly delighted; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Seal of Immeasurability of the Illusion-like Samādhi Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll II.
